CONTROL 1 -- planar closed curve, Wr must be exactly 0
CONTROL 2 -- two INDEPENDENT writhe algorithms must agree
The obvious test -- 'a figure-eight has Wr = 1' -- is FALSE: writhe is geometric, not
topological, so a loosely crossed lemniscate has whatever its shape gives it. The first
version of this file asserted it, measured 0.388, and recorded a FAIL against correct code.
So: solid angle against averaged signed crossings, sharing no code.

CONTROL 3 -- THE ONE THAT MATTERS. Lk must survive refine and coarsen exactly.
A leak here does not blow up; it drifts, and drifting supercoiling looks like physics.

CONTROL 4 -- is the twist physical? Wr changes with shape, and Tw must move to match.
This is the supercoiling mechanism itself: at fixed Lk, writhing a rod UNTWISTS it.

PASS  planar Wr = 0

The topology layer holds. Refinement moves Wr by a real amount -- the polygon genuinely
changes -- and the twist absorbs it, so Lk is invariant to 4e-16 across eight successive
resolution changes. That was the flagged risk in the architecture and it is now a test
rather than a hope. The KMC and melting tiers can be built on this.
